rules.statement: In an agent autopilot workflow's instructions, never let a follow-up become an unattended fix step when its fix would edit a protected path (CI workflows, `.github`, `.claude`, build scripts, dependency manifests or lock files), whoever wrote the follow-up line and whether or not it carries a review-thread URL; file it or list it for the maintainer instead.
rules.why: Follow-up text can come from issue bodies or reworded bot findings, both of which can carry prompt injection. A guard that only applies to some origins, such as lines ending in a thread URL, lets an injected line edit CI or agent config and push it unattended.
rules.check: Look for a protected-path refusal that depends on a condition about where the line came from (has a thread URL, written by the planner, added by a review) rather than applying to every follow-up-derived step, and for follow-up steps that skip the protected-path or Done-when rules other steps follow.

rules.statement: In an agent autopilot workflow's instructions, run the post-step protected-path diff check on every step an unattended run makes, and don't exempt steps by origin, such as those built from the plan's own follow-ups. The only allowed exception is a path the maintainer named explicitly.
rules.why: The diff check is the backstop that stops an unattended run from pushing edits to CI, hooks or agent config. If any class of step is exempt, the backstop has a hole an injected follow-up can get through.
rules.check: Look for wording that makes the protected-path diff check skip some paths or steps, or that drops the check after a fix-follow-ups round. Confirm the check runs after every round of automated steps.
